She was gang raped severally by some bad boys and that made her become so lonely to herself and always sad. Prince Richærd, who had come back to the village from abroad, returned to marry his half-caste chatterbox girlfriend when he met Sophia At first, he had thought it was mere pity, he had thought he was just being emotional till he decided to bring her and her mother to his house, that was when he found out he was really falling in love. He was ready to do everything possible to make her see. That great bond of love helped to reveal Sophia’s true identity and some secrets behind her blindness. On a cool morning after a thorough surgery, Sophia was able to see again. She was happy to be able to see her love not knowing there were many odds against her. Many secrets that could break their bond. Many enemies to destroy their love. For Sophia to be with Richærd, she must be ready to face the battle. Don’t miss this sorrowful r0mance book. Are you really enthusiastic to unravel the mysteries behind the mysteries? Chapter 1 Should have k-ssed you Should have touched you Should have hugged you You mean everything to me My joy, my perfection, my sadness lessen anytime you’re around Sophia’s POV ” Where is my stick? ” I asked no one in particular as I stop singing, I felt no joy singing but I just did to keep myself busy. I can’t see anyone anyway? I’m clouded with darkness, I can’t tell if anyone was hearing me, I don’t know if there was anyone around. ” Can someone help me find my stick, it just dropped off my grip now ” I bawled with tears forming in my eyes as I moved my hand all over the floor in search of it. You can’t tell how frustrated I am right now. I think my mom isn’t around because she is the only one that hears my cry, she is the only one I have. My dad and step mother are the thorns in my flesh, I don’t know how anyone of them looks like but I can tell their voices and feels it whenever I’m with any of them, with their shout and baleful acts towards me, I would know they are the one. Not one of them likes me a bit, they don’t mind beating me together, To them and most of the people around, I’m cursed. I was hated not just by my family but most of the people around I had stopped school when I couldn’t bear the scorn anymore. It was real hell, hatred was all that surrounded me. The only person that loves me is my mother but she doesn’t stay around always, she is always striving for what we would eat I can’t say I have a dad because he doesn’t feed us anymore.. All these plight are as a result of my blindness from birth. ” You are a disgrace to me and I feels ashamed to the fact that you are my daughter!!” That has always been my father’s word to me. I feel like taking my life but I wouldn’t because my mom still needs me. I would have committed suicide if she isn’t in my life because without her, my life is useless and I’m better dead than alive. “Please someone should help ” I s¢ræmed with a heavy heart. ” Who is that blind bastard making noise around the neighbourhood ” The growl of my step mom resounded in my ear sending shrills down my spine.. “Please where is my mom?” I asked “Are you asking me?..like seriously, you are asking me where your mother is, I’m I the one who caused your blindness?.. please I should hear word in this house..” She scoffed. ” Erm.. please help me find my stick, please ” I stupidly asked even when I knew she would never do it. “Okay ma ” She said and I was happy and surprised that she wanted to help. “Take ” She said and I started waving my hand over the space. “Where is it? ” I asked frustrated. ” Take it here ” She said with a giggle and I kept moving my hand searching for where she was but couldn’t touch anything. She burst Into a hysterical laughter and that was when it dawned on me that she was just pouring scorn on me. I sighed and pushed back my tears then located a seat with my hand. I made to seat down but she dragged the seat away making me fall on my butt. ” Why are you doing this ” I squealed with my heart aching badly You can’t tell the kind of hurt I feel right now, not just from the fall but from the fact that I was been maltreated by someone who should help me. ” Stay there on the floor till your wretched mother comes back,, disgusting fellow ” She spited and stomped out. Tears fell off my eyes as I felt totally drained, when would all this end? When would I regain my sight? When would I be loved by the people I meet. You can’t tell how pained I am. Words can’t explain it. ” Omg .. Summer, what are you doing there on the floor ” I heard my mom’s voice cooed. She hastily, helped me up and lead me to the bed. ” What happened? ” She asked with her voice cracking with emotions. ” My step mom is at it again.. but please mom I’m very hungry ” I muffled ” Open your mouth ” she said and I obliged. She pushed in a substance into my mouth, I don’t even know the name.. It was sweet so I munched it and opened mouth to get more but nothing came into my mouth. ” I’m sorry daughter, that’s all I could get, no one helped me, no one wanted to have any thing to do with me.. ” They said i was a cursed mother because I bore you ” She said sniffing back her tears. I can sense pain and hurt in her voice. ” I’m no more hungry, stop crying ” I said in a cracked voice.. She was really going through a lot cos of me I know how it could be like having everyone turning against you. ” Please manage that, I promise tomorrow would be better ” she cried and I nodded with a smile. Just then, my stomach made a grumbling sound.. ” Oh you are really hungry, I think I need to go beg your father for some money ” She said and I held her. ” No..no ,, I’m sure you are aware he wouldn’t, you are going their to receive scorn and insult and possibly beating ” I said pitifully and she sighed and fondle my cheek. ” I don’t mind taking all that for you, who knows he may have mercy ” she said and left. I sat there feeling sober. I hate my life, there was no single thing to make me happy. Pain, anguish, sorrow sadness ,all these are all that keeps looming all around me. No one shows me love a single bit, I don’t know how I look, how human looks like is even vague in my memory. I hate my life like mad, I wish death would take me away at this moment, I don’t want to try killing myself again but I want to die. Maybe when I die, my mother’s sorrow would decrease. The only advice she had been receiving from everyone was to kill that curse which was me. They keeps telling her to kill me so that they would accept her back, I was like a burden to her. Many time, I had tried killing myself but someway somehow, she would still save me. I had once walked out of the house without my stick or assistant praying something would hit me and I would die. It was just like death dreads me a lot because it couldn’t come near me. I wish for death but it isn’t coming even after the depression and torture from my dad who seem to hate me more than anyone else. I was still in thought when i felt my mother running to where I was. ” Mom is that you?,, what? ” I couldn’t finish my statement when something hit my head so hærdly that I felt blood dripping out. ” Omg!,, why did you do that , Oh gosh, you are so wicked ” My mother cried as she helped me up. “You got to tell me how you came here and what your mission is, you are not a human… You are a curse and have been my reason for every single badluck i had gotten all through my life” I heard the voice of my dad growl. That voice I dreaded a lot. Pain was all I felt but it wasn’t compared to the one I felt when he slapped my mother. “Don’t you ever come to me for money to feed this badluck and misfortune, next time you try it, I’ll make sure I skin you alive ” He yelled and stomped out. ” Mother please kill me, please” I pleaded with tears flowing like a stream. ” I would be the most evil monster to do that, if you should die then death should take you away, I would never kill my daughter ” She sobbed. ” If you don’t, I will do it myself..one day, I will get hold of a knife or any sharp object and i will rip my heart heart with it ” I said in tears and pain. ” I’ll never allow you do any harm to yourself ” She cooed hugging me tightly. ” Can we leave this place? ” I asked and she sniffed. ” I would have take you away from here if I could ” She cried more bitterly making the urge to kill myself increase. ” Why would I be a burden to an innocent soul, a child was suppose to be a relief to the mother but here I am making her get much more torture and agony ” I said ” Seat down let me dress your wound ” she said moving her hand to my head. I quickly shoved her hand away angrily. ” Let it bleed, leave it, let me bleed to death ” I bawled with tears. ” Shut up and seat down ” She half yelled and I held my shoulder to direct me to the seat but to her surprise, I held her hand and shoved her away from my body.. “Allow me to die ” I s¢ræmed and ran away to where I am not seeing. I can’t wait to hit my head on the wall and die. ” Noooo..no..stop.. No ” Her voice hitched as I slammed my head on the wall and fell flatly on the floor. Death please come, I f*cking need you now.

But so do consistency, honesty, accountability, respect, communication, consideration, and reciprocal effort. Someone doesn’t need to be perfect to love you well. But you shouldn’t have to repeatedly convince someone that your basic emotional needs matter. The goal of this book isn’t to tell you what decision to make. name: THE FIRST 60 DAYS OF YOUR NEW BUSINESS (NEW BUSINESS FOUNDATION HANDBOOK) .ebook
description: THE FIRST 60 DAYS OF YOUR NEW BUSINESS — EBOOK (PDF) THE FIRST 60 DAYS OF YOUR NEW BUSINESS takes you into the decisions that happen beneath the excitement of starting a business—the decisions that rarely look dangerous when you're making them, but can quietly determine what the business becomes later. There is a reason the book focuses specifically on sixty days. During those early weeks, you're not only building a business. The business is building you. Your spending habits. Your financial habits. Your response to uncertainty. Your attitude toward slow sales. Your relationship with risk. Your standards for the people you trust. Your willingness to look at uncomfortable numbers. Your daily routines. Repeated long enough, these things stop feeling like decisions. They become the way you operate. And some of the lessons in those first weeks are not obvious. What happens when your first meaningful profit arrives? Why might spending that money feel completely justified—and still be one of the worst decisions you could make? Why can a business show impressive revenue while its actual financial position is much weaker? Why can a seemingly attractive partnership become a problem only after the excitement has disappeared? Why can a friend be trustworthy personally and still be the wrong person for an important business responsibility? And what happens when fear convinces you that a temporary setback is actually proof that your business cannot succeed? These are the kinds of questions this book forces you to look at before they become expensive. You will also discover why some of the most important business practices are remarkably ordinary. Recording the money. Checking the numbers. Following up with customers. Reviewing the day. Protecting working capital. Questioning an opportunity. Delaying a purchase. Repeating the routine. None of these actions looks like a breakthrough. But the book explores what happens when they are practiced consistently during the period when your business is still forming its identity. And then there is David. He starts with limited savings and a secondhand printer. His business gets its first significant sale. An attractive partnership opportunity appears. Then sales slow down. Each moment gives him a reason to make a different decision. What he does next reveals something important about how a business can be strengthened—or quietly weakened—long before its problems become visible. Inside this book, you'll discover: The early business habits that can quietly follow you for years. Why your first profit can create a temptation you may not recognize. The difference between revenue, profit, and cash flow that many new entrepreneurs misunderstand. Why your financial records may be telling you something your intuition isn't. The emotional traps hidden inside excitement, fear, pride, and impatience. Why some opportunities should make you slow down instead of move faster. What you should look for before trusting someone with an important part of your business. Why a written agreement can protect a partnership rather than weaken it. How seemingly insignificant routines can become the operating system of a growing business. And why the habits you establish while nobody is watching may eventually become the strongest—or weakest—part of your business. This isn't a book about pretending you know everything. It is about seeing what you might otherwise miss while there is still time to change it. Because the expensive mistake is not always the obviously foolish one. Sometimes it's the decision that makes perfect sense today. Sometimes it's the opportunity that looks too good to question. Sometimes it's the person you trust without checking. On the flip side, his relationship is hitting the rocks, as his lover is stalling on a reply after seven months. At home, he's having a hard time dealing with his father's erratic insults which gives him traumatic episodes and a low self esteem as he struggles to find his place between adolescence, teen age, and adulthood. Locked in the middle of his life, his love, and his emotions, he takes a decision no one expected of him or saw coming. According to the World Health Organization, approximately one million people die each year from suicide and suicide related causes, resulting in about one death by suicide every eleven minutes globally. With the same statistics narrowing it down to at least one person committing suicide every 40 seconds, as at year 2020. In Nigeria in particular, the clusters of suicidal cases amongst several teenagers, youths, and few concerning adult like the Osapa London tragedy, raises awareness to the fact that many are experiencing emotional trauma, family dysfunction, relationship crisis, mental disorder (amongst others), and are in dire need of help. And sadly, in Nigeria, we address issues from the roof, not the root. Especially when it comes to matters of having someone to talk to, someone to listen to us, therapy, and everything that has to do with suicide and mental health conversations. It is to this purpose that I am introducing you to DEAREST SUICIDE BOOK 2...Sometimes, DEATH becomes the only option. ******************************************************* SO, WHAT IS IT FOR ME IN THIS BOOK?? Dearest Suicide is a coming-of-age, controversial, and evergreen book that is a must-read for every teenager, youth, and adult of all ages, class, and status. The book covers different areas and scope of the average adolescent and contemporary adult, from relationship, to sex, academics, religion, emotions, family life, work life, and breakups (breakfast). This is a book that should be in every school and on every book shelf, as it reveals deep-seated truths and sick realities the society continuously shies away from, frowns at, and fails to talk about, when it comes to suicide. There is vast amount of information from the book which can be applied to a number of human situations, not just suicide, and help people who have been hurting a long time, struggling with people who hurt them, or who are currently hurting. With the 2022 World Suicide Prevention Day coming up on September 10, the timing of such a well-written-sensitive-yet-controversial subject could not be more perfect. It will show you how great individuals, important celebrities and amiable personalities across the globe have either taken or attempted to take their lives in view of the harsh difficulties and telling situations travailing their human existence, giving you an insight and knowledge into understanding each person’s story and having the right conversations in specific places. You are about to experience twists, turns, intrigues, suspense, anguish, tension, crises, counter plots, and epic clashes, in this story with several parts: a depressive-romantic thriller, a teenage crisis, a family roller coaster, a self-help manual, and a real-time relationship saga, amongst other telling, engaging, scourging, and provoking tales. And as you progress in each chapter, you will be conditioned to refer back to his disclaimer and warm advice time and time again. THIS ISN’T A FICTION. THIS IS REALITY! ******************************************************* WHAT PEOPLE ARE SAYING CONCERNING DEAREST SUICIDE… DR. OREOFE WILLIAMS | President, OREOFE FILMS; Arch mentor, City of Talents Worldwide You are a fantastic writer and as a literary fellow myself, I am extremely proud of your contributions to humanities. Your art is bold and unapologetically satirical. You don't actually write, you craft. And crafting is what makes a great writer. Perhaps this could be published, who knows? If I had read PaGidi's Dearest Suicide at the time, I probably would not have made such a bold claim. This book totally redefines those terms. Dearest Suicide will come off as many things to different people. But to me, it's a heartfelt conversation with a new friend, a firsthand account of what really went down, and most of all, it's one of the most detailed histories and accounts of suicide I've read in one piece. I did not want it to end. name: Kingston Ventura - The V.I.C.E Hook Framework
description: For Copywriters, Creative Strategists, Media Buyers, and Short-Form Content Creators Who Are Tired of Writing Hooks That Feel Right and Die in the Feed… Engineer Hooks That Stop the Scroll in 2 Seconds Flat — Using a 3-Layer Diagnostic System That Tells You Exactly Why Any First Line Works or Dies Before You Ship It WITHOUT Guesswork, Swipe Files, or Another Round of Split Testing You Can't Explain Today, every hook you've ever written that died in the feed will suddenly make sense. Every "make it pop" note from a client that left you with nothing to say will have an answer. And every first line you write from this point forward will get built — not guessed. If you're a copywriter… This one shift will tell you exactly why your hooks are inconsistent — even when you're doing everything right — and hand you the diagnostic that makes inconsistency structurally impossible. If you're a creative strategist or media buyer… This is the fastest way I know to stop testing your way to a winning hook and start *engineering* your way there — cutting your testing cycles in half while producing first lines that hold longer and convert harder. Because the problem isn't your instincts. The problem runs much deeper than that. Because I'm not just talking about curiosity gaps. Not open loops. Not power words. Not "emotionally charged language" as a concept you already know you're supposed to use. Those are ingredients without a recipe. When the best-performing hooks in DTC advertising were reverse-engineered… What emerged was a three-layer architecture. And here's the part that will make you uncomfortable: Every single one of those hooks had all three layers present. The hooks that died — including many written by talented, experienced practitioners — were missing at least one. Not weak. Not poorly written. Incomplete. You Can't Win an Engineering Game By Playing an Instinct Game. You need to understand what your hook is actually doing before the reader processes a single word. You need to understand why the emotional charge in a first line detonates in the body before it registers in the brain — and which specific language mechanisms trigger that response and which ones kill it. You need to understand the architectural difference between a hook that creates curiosity and a hook that creates COMPULSION. And you need to be able to calibrate the believability of your claim with enough precision that it lands in the exact window where it sounds almost too good to be true — but doesn't tip over the edge into rejection. None of that is instinct. All of it is learnable. And none of it has ever been packaged into a single system. Until now. Think about what this actually costs you when you get it wrong. You write the hook. It feels solid. You ship it. You refresh the metrics at 11am. The two-second hold rate is low. People are clicking off before the setup lands. The algorithm is already deprioritizing the placement. You have a campaign running on a hook that never had a CHANCE… And you can't explain to your client, your team, or yourself exactly what went wrong. So you write more variants. You test more. You study competitor ads. And occasionally something lands, and you celebrate — but you can't fully explain why. Which means you can't replicate it. That is not a skill problem. That is a diagnostic problem. You don't have a system for identifying which of the three layers is missing. So you're fixing symptoms instead of architecture. You've been doing this long enough that the inconsistency feels like a personal indictment. Maybe the copywriters who can write hooks on command have something you don't. Maybe this is just luck dressed up as craft. It isn't. Your hook isn't weak. It's incomplete. The highest-converting hooks in any market — any format, any channel — share three properties. Every single one of them. Without exception. Most practitioners write hooks with one of those properties present, occasionally two, rarely all three. The practitioner who can reliably build all three layers simultaneously doesn't need luck, doesn't need volume testing, and doesn't need to study the competitor's ad and wonder what they did. They know what was done. They can name it. They can rebuild it. And they can do it again. That is what shifts you from a Hook Guesser to a Hook Engineer. And when you make that shift… You don't just write better hooks. You become the person in the room who can look at any first line — yours, a client's, a competitor's — run it through the diagnostic, and tell the room exactly which layer is broken and precisely how to rebuild it. That is a different kind of value than "good copywriter." That is the kind of value that commands different fees, different authority, and different respect. Imagine that. Being the person who, when a creative review stalls because something is "off" and nobody can name what it is — walks to the whiteboard and explains it with engineering precision. Not because you got lucky. Because you built it right. For months, every high-performing hook that could be identified and analyzed was pulled apart. Campaigns generating $100 million or more in tracked sales. Short-form content at 14 million, 46 million, and 5 million views. Hundreds of split-tested variants across fitness, finance, beauty, info-products, and e-commerce… The private creative standards of a former CMO inside Hormozi's portfolio — a person who required that every single ad passing through their review meet one standard above all others. That standard was a single word. That word became the first layer of the framework. What emerged from all of it wasn't a template. It wasn't a swipe file. It wasn't a list of tactics that work sometimes. It was a pattern. Present in every winning hook. Absent in every hook that died. Three layers. Always three. Never fewer. Every winning hook had all of them. Every dead hook was missing at least one. That pattern has been named, sequenced, and made teachable for the first time. Introducing… THE V.I.C.E. HOOK FRAMEWORK Visceral · Irresistible · Contrast-Engineered The V.I.C.E. Hook Framework is the complete 3-layer diagnostic and construction system that makes the difference between a hook that works and a hook that dies not a matter of taste, talent, or luck. It's a matter of architecture. The feed is getting more crowded every 90 days. AI is producing more content volume than the entire internet held in 2010 — every single week. In this environment, the average hook doesn't just underperform. It's invisible. A decent hook written by a competent practitioner used to be enough. AI produces decent hooks in three seconds now. Decent is worthless. The only hooks that work are the ones that feel dangerous, specific, and human in the first line. The ones that detonate before the reader has decided whether to keep watching. The ones built on all three layers. The V.I.C.E. Framework was built for this reality — not the reality of 2018. Master it now and you're not just writing better first lines. You're building a skill that becomes more valuable the noisier the feed gets. Because everyone else is producing volume. You'll be producing architecture. Whether You're… ✅ A freelance copywriter: Use the V.I.C.E. diagnostic to audit any client hook in under five minutes — and deliver a layer-by-layer breakdown that positions you as a strategic partner, not a word-arranger. That repositioning is worth more in a single project than the cost of this framework. ✅ A DTC brand media buyer: Write ten hook variants calibrated to specific points on the Believability Scale and know exactly which tier to test first — instead of running equal-weight tests across hooks that were never architecturally sound to begin with. ✅ A short-form content creator: Align all four hook channels before you film so editing doesn't become a rescue operation. The Spoken, Visual, Text, and Audio alignment check takes four minutes before production and saves four hours after. ✅ A creative strategist inside an agency: Use V.I.C.E. as a shared diagnostic language across your team. Score every hook before it ships. End the "something feels off" conversation forever. ✅ A solopreneur or coach: Write organic content hooks that build authority without ad spend — using the same three-layer architecture that powers eight-figure DTC campaigns, scaled down to a single post. Here's What's Inside The V.I.C.E. Hook Framework ☑ A word-level rewrite technique, used instinctively by every top-performing direct response copywriter in the last 100 years, that replaces Latin-root and French-root clinical language with short, earthy, body-level words that hit the nervous system before the brain has time to evaluate them. Run this principle on any hook you've written in the last month and you'll see immediately why certain lines landed and others didn't — without changing a single idea. ☑ A consequence-first rewrite framework that restructures any hook so the reader feels what happens to *them* before you've introduced the mechanism, the product, or the proof — the same architectural principle that separates the opening lines of every high-converting VSL from the ones that bleed viewers in the first 8 seconds. ☑ A pre-production diagnostic that synchronizes Spoken, Visual, Text, and Audio across any short-form video hook so misalignment across channels can't silently kill a first line that read perfectly on the page. Most hook training teaches one channel. This checklist covers all four in under four minutes. ☑ Exactly how to engineer Stated Contrast vs. Implied Contrast in your hook — so you can choose, with precision, whether to name both the common belief AND the contrarian reality explicitly, or introduce the contrarian reality alone and let the reader construct the baseline themselves — and why picking the wrong contrast type for your audience's awareness level is one of the most common reasons technically solid hooks still die. ☑ A declassified creative standard from inside one of the highest-performing direct response organizations in the world — a former CMO's single-word requirement for every ad before it could ship — that captures the entire emotional philosophy of Layer 1 in one visceral syllable. The moment you read this word, you will immediately re-evaluate every hook you've written in the last three years. ☑ The diagnostic for identifying exactly where your hook actually begins inside the copy you're currently writing, and how to strip the warmup, the context-setting, and the credential-establishing so your real first line is the first line your reader sees. Applied to most copy in this market, this single audit cuts the dead weight from the opening and doubles the emotional charge of what remains. ☑ How David Ogilvy's research obsession — his insistence on spending more time studying the reader than writing to them — maps directly onto the contrast-engineering principle in Layer 2, and why the copywriters who've studied his methods but missed this specific application are building curiosity loops with the wrong baseline belief as their anchor. ☑ A worked example tracing the same hook concept through seven different calibration levels, showing exactly what the language looks like — so you can feel the difference between a claim that excites and a claim that triggers rejection before you've ever run a single test. ☑ The specific structural and tonal properties that make a hook feel like something the reader discovered rather than something they were served, and why hooks that trigger the "this is an ad" signal in the first line lose 60–80% of their potential audience before the second sentence. This is not about being subtle. It's about being architecturally different from what trained ad-skepticism is looking for. ☑ Exactly how to use the Qualified Contrast Test to determine, before you write a single word, whether your hook's central idea has enough distance from the reader's existing belief to create genuine curiosity — or whether you're about to spend an hour crafting a first line that confirms what they already think and gives them no reason to keep reading. ☑ Exactly how to run the full V.I.C.E. diagnostic on any hook in under 8 minutes — Layer 1 checklist, Layer 2 architecture review, Layer 3 Believability calibration, four-channel alignment confirmation — so you can audit a client's hook before a creative review, rebuild the failing layer on the spot, and deliver a precision diagnosis that no one in the room can argue with because it's systematic, not subjective. ☑ ⚠️ WARNING: The "open loop" advice that dominates hook training right now — the idea that creating a curiosity gap is sufficient to stop the scroll — is a partial truth that becomes actively dangerous when it's the only principle being applied. An open loop without emotional viciousness is a door with no room behind it. Here's what happens to your hold rate when curiosity is present but Layer 1 is missing — and why this combination produces the most frustrating failure mode in copywriting: technically correct hooks that consistently underperform. ☑ How the FBI's behavioral analysis unit uses consequence-first framing in high-stakes interrogation openings — leading with what has already happened to the subject before introducing any mechanism, explanation, or ask — and how this same architecture, applied to your hook's opening line, triggers the same neurological attention response in a viewer that it triggers in a subject who suddenly realizes the stakes are real. ☑ The 3 most common Layer failures that kill hooks written by experienced copywriters — and why each one feels like a different problem when it's actually the same diagnostic issue viewed from three different angles. Identifying which failure mode you default to is the fastest path to systematic improvement. ☑ ⚠️ WARNING: If you are currently using AI to generate hook variants and selecting winners by gut feel, you are combining the most efficient hook-production tool ever created with the least reliable selection methodology — and producing high volume at low accuracy. Here's how to use the V.I.C.E. diagnostic as an AI hook filter: prompt for volume, score by layer, ship only what passes all three gates. ☑ The specific type of stakes language that triggers involuntary attention the same way a car accident stops traffic, and the line between stakes that create compulsive engagement and stakes that create anxiety and avoidance. Understanding this line is the difference between a hook that makes a viewer lean in and one that makes them scroll faster to get away from it. And that's just scratching the surface... description: THE SHADOWED HEART SAGA: BOOK 1 Obsidian Huntress: Grave of Thorns and Stars To break the curse, she must deliver the High Lord's heart. To survive, she must first escape his gravity. Elara is the kingdom’s greatest weapon: the Obsidian Huntress, a woman whose very touch is poison to the deceitful Fae. Bound by a vicious Blood Debt Curse from the human King Valerius, her mission is simple: infiltrate the treacherous Court of Nyxos and assassinate its High Lord, Kaelen. Failure means not only her death but the annihilation of her entire village. But High Lord Kaelen is not the monster she was promised. He is a master of shadows, infuriatingly charismatic, and dangerously perceptive. Every shared glance feels like a challenge, and the forbidden tension between them threatens to shatter her resolve and condemn her soul. As she closes in on her target, Elara is struck by a truth more volatile than any Fae magic: she is not just a human tool, but the last living member of the legendary Star-Seer lineage, a power capable of razing entire courts. When her mission collapses, Elara finds herself Kaelen’s unwilling captive, the Blood Debt still coiled around her heart, and the human king preparing for war. Now trapped in a realm of infinite night and ancient malice, Elara must decide if she will use her newfound power to destroy the Fae who captured her, or join him to save a world that never wanted her. Obsidian Huntress: Grave of Thorns and Stars is the first book in the high-stakes, enemies-to-lovers fantasy romance The Shadowed Heart Saga, perfect for readers who crave dangerous Fae, dark court politics, and morally gray heroes.

description: He built the perfect city. Now, he has to tear it down. In the hyper-capitalist metropolis of Veridia, efficiency is god, and the Aura Spire is its temple. Armed with a stolen face, a crew of mechanics and rebels, and a mind that sees the fracture line in every structure, Klaus must ascend the Spire one last time. He isn't going up to reclaim his life. Definition of Dropshipping Dropshipping is a type of order fulfillment where store owners don’t manage inventory themselves. Instead, dropshippers buy the items from a third-party supplier who fulfills customers’ orders for them. AN EXAMPLE OF DROPSHIPPING Let’s imagine you have an online store where you sell watch products. As a dropshipper, you don’t need to buy hundreds or thousands of watches in advance and store them in a rented warehouse (or your garage) until you make a sale. Instead, you find a third-party vendor who has the warehouse space to stock your items. Once a customer purchases from you, your supplier (or suppliers, there can be many of them), takes over the process and ships the product directly to your customer. You never need to deal with packaging and logistics! Your main task as a seller is to list your products on your dropshipping store, do marketing for your dropshipping store, get the customers to your store, You can do that from anywhere as long as you have a smartphone or laptop and internet connection! ARE DROPSHIPPING COMPANIES PROFITABLE? Today, dropshipping is a legit business model that can help you earn $10k in two months or more once you get the hang of it! The sky is your limit. Dropshipping works so well that more than 33% of online stores use it to fulfill their product demand. Dropshipping is projected to be a $591.77 billion industry by 2027. How do you get a piece of that? How do you carve your slice from this multi billion dollar industry? Let’s go to an imaginary dog product store. Let’s imagine that one of the products in your store is this orthopedic dog bed. You can buy this bed on AliExpress for as low as $8.45. You sell it for $39 in your online store and shipping and advertising costs you $9 per product (most customers expect free shipping, so we advise including the shipping costs in the price of the product). Let’s count your profit: $39 - $8.45 - $9 = $21.55 per product If you want to make over $10,000 per month, you need to sell about 464 of these dog beds. You don’t need a fancy degree from a business school or large sums of money to enter the market. BENEFITS OF DROPSHIPPING Here are the reasons why you will enjoy being a dropshipper. 1. It’s very easy to get started with dropshipping. Once you’ve found quality products, you can launch your first dropshipping store in a couple of hours. As your business grows, you may want to invest more into your marketing to get even more sales, but the nature of your daily tasks won’t change much in general. 5. As a dropshipper, you can sell your products anywhere in the world as long as the shipping costs are worth it. 6. THE SUPPLY CHAIN CONSISTS OF THREE PARTIES: Manufacturer: the creator of the products you dropship; sells those items in large quantities to suppliers and wholesalers. If you want to, you can get your products shipped directly from manufacturers. For example, instead of going to AliExpress to look for suppliers, you can contact manufacturers at Alibaba. This way, you will pay less for your products because you skip the supplier. You’ll also be able to customize your branding a little too. Supplier/wholesaler: the person who buys products from manufacturers and sells them to retailers (dropshippers). Suppliers usually specialize in a particular niche, making it easy for you to find the items you want to sell. They mark up the products a little. name: The ultimate book of sales techniques _ 75 ways to master cold calling, sharpen your unique selling proposition, and close the sale
description: Your biggest competitor is the status quo. This book contains my top tips for salespeople, honed and refined over the years. In many ways it’s the ultimate product of more than three decades in this business. It’s the result of training more than half-a-million salespeople, of going on thousands of sales calls, and of making hundreds of thousands of phone calls. Yet in this book, I can tell you nothing—nothing—that’s more important than this: Your biggest competitor is the status quo. That’s what you have to overcome. I mean this in two senses. The first, which I’ve drummed into salespeople for a long time is simple. The prospect to whom you’re talking during your sales appointment or your cold call is happy with what he’s got. He has no defined need. If he did, if he wasn’t happy, he’d have called you. Salespeople are often taught to look for problems, or even create them. That’s bunk. For the most part, if a customer has a problem, she or he will resolve it themselves. Instead of this problem-centric approach, look at things this way: What you’re fighting against is whatever way the customer’s accustomed to doing things, whatever service he’s using, whatever product he’s employing. From his point of view, the status quo seems to be working; your job is to help him understand why it isn’t. You have to change him from what he’s doing (even if it appears to be nothing) to what you want him to do. You have to change him. I’ll talk a great deal about this problem of the status quo and how to overcome it. It’s key to creating an effective cold call and a killer sales pitch. These days, when I’m addressing groups of salespeople a lot of what I talk about focuses on innovation—a key word. Innovation, after all, is what separates you from the rest of the pack. It’s what makes the difference between good and great. Ninety-nine percent of us these days are selling a commodity product! What will get you the sale in the face of this is the degree of your creativity. If you look the same as the other salespeople who are trying to sell essentially the same thing as you, you’ll get nowhere. To spark that creativity, you’ve got to have insight into the customer: what they do, how they do it, when they do it, whom they do it with, and perhaps most importantly, why they do it that way. Once you understand that, you can find innovative ways of showing them how you can help them do it better. People buy because they believe that what you’re selling is better than what they currently have. Your challenge is to demonstrate that fact to them. And how can you possibly do that unless you understand what they’re doing with the product or service they’re currently using? The answer is, you can’t. Hence the value of insight. Keep these words in mind as you read through the chapters that follow: insight … creativity … innovation … different.

name: UNFADING MIND: Book 5-THE SENSORY EDITION Hearing, Vision, and the Brain's Survival— Protecting Your Senses, Strengthening Your Mind, and Building Lifelong Cognitive Clarity
description: They told you it was just your eyes. They told you it was just your ears. They were wrong. Hearing loss and vision decline are not simply inconveniences of aging. They are neurological emergencies in slow motion, and the research is now unambiguous. Adults with untreated hearing loss are up to five times more likely to develop dementia. Vision impairment doubles the risk of cognitive decline. Every sense you lose is a pipeline of information your brain depended on to stay sharp, stay connected, and stay alive to the world around it. The brain does not just receive what your senses deliver. It is built by it. And when that input fades, the brain begins to shrink. This is the book that tells you what your doctor’s appointment never had time to explain. What is actually happening inside the aging brain when senses decline? When hearing fades, the brain reallocates cognitive resources just to process sound, stealing bandwidth from memory, attention, and executive thinking. When vision dims, spatial awareness, balance, emotional recognition, and social connection all quietly deteriorate alongside it. The brain compensates, exhausts itself compensating, and eventually stops compensating at all. The tragedy is not the decline itself. The tragedy is that most of it is preventable, manageable, and reversible, if you know what to do and when to do it. Most people wait too long. They normalize the changes. They adjust. They withdraw from conversations that are too hard to follow. They stop driving. They stop going out. They tell themselves it is fine. It is not fine. And this book will not let you settle for fine. Unfading Mind: Hearing, Vision, and the Brain’s Survival is the Sensory Specialized Edition of the Unfading Mind Series — the only cognitive health library built specifically for aging adults, caregivers, and everyone who refuses to watch a brilliant mind fade without a fight. Inside, you will find: ∙ The science of how hearing and vision loss directly trigger and accelerate cognitive decline ∙ Why the brain shrinks in regions tied to memory and thinking when sensory input is lost ∙ The critical intervention windows , when action protects the brain and when waiting costs you ∙ How to identify early sensory decline before it becomes irreversible damage ∙ A complete Sensory Protection Protocol covering hearing, vision, and the brain’s response to both ∙ The hidden connection between sensory isolation, depression, and dementia ∙ How caregivers can recognize, address, and slow sensory decline in a loved one ∙ The integrated workbook guide for building daily habits that protect your senses and your mind This is not about getting hearing aids or stronger glasses. This is about understanding that your senses are the brain’s lifeline, and protecting them is one of the most powerful cognitive health decisions you will ever make. You have already lost some ground. Everyone has. The question is what you do next. This book is your answer. Part of the Unfading Mind Series Book 1: Protecting Memory, Thinking Skills, and Independence in an Aging Brain Book 2: The Longevity Protocol Book 3: The Caregiver’s Guide Sleep Edition | Sensory Edition: Hearing, Vision, and the Brain’s Survival Emotional Health Edition

name: The Everything Creative Writing Book_ All you need to know to write novels, plays, short stories, screenplays, poems, articles, or blogs
description: You love reading. You’ve done a little bit of writing. And you’ve often wondered if you could be a writer like the incredibly creative authors you admire, but you’re not quite sure where to start. If you have the interest and the desire to become a more creative writer—and it’s looking like you do—and if you are willing to take the time to learn and practice, this book can show you how to improve your writing skills and express yourself imaginatively in a variety of ways. With dedication, skill building, and time, it’s entirely possible that you could become another Nora Roberts, E. B. White, Toni Morrison, Dean Koontz, Sue Grafton, or Nicholas Sparks. You could develop a style so expressive, so true, and so yours, that whenever someone reads something that you wrote, he or she might wish, like Holden Caulfield in The Catcher in the Rye, that “when you’re all done reading it, you wish the author that wrote it was a terrific friend of yours and you could call him up on the phone whenever you felt like it.” You could succeed as a creative writer beyond your wildest, best selling author, cross-country-book-signing dreams. But you could also fail. You could put in the time, tell everyone you know that you’re working to become a writer, write and write and write, and still not get published. The thought is daunting, to say the least. But there’s still another possible drawback. While you’re courageously giving this writing thing your all, you could run into resistance instead of reinforcement. Friends, colleagues, parents, children, even your partner or your spouse might try to discourage you by telling you what you already know: that you could fail, that you could get your feelings hurt, that you might not have what it takes. Such disheartening counsel, whether spoken to spare you pain or from jealousy disguised as caring, can give an author a terminal case of writer’s block. So why try to do it? Why not just carry on quietly and safely behind the perfectly useful and perfectly ordinary words that many people set down on paper when they must write something—in their business documents, their personal correspondence, perhaps in an occasional journal entry or school paper or speech? Because you love words. Because you feel you have something to say and you’d like to say it in the best possible, most interesting way. Because you love to communicate and connect with all kinds of people. Because you find joy in the colors, tastes, rhythms, and smells of language. Because you have opinions, experiences, and feelings that you need to share with your readers. Because you want to explore and question and make sense of what you see around you, and help others to do the same. Because you see things in a special way. By giving your love of language a chance to blossom and grow, and by setting a goal of becoming an accomplished creative writer, you might one day find yourself in a Manhattan bookstore, signing your name on hundreds of copies of your latest biography. Or perhaps you’ll be watching a sold-out performance of a play that you penned. Or maybe the story you got published in a major magazine will earn you a hefty check. All those things could happen. But what will definitely happen when you make the commitment to write more creatively is that you’ll learn new skills, gain new knowledge, and find new ways to express yourself—even if you “fail” and not a word that you write is ever published. Learning and growing will expand your horizons and increase your abilities, give you an amazing feeling of well-being and fulfillment, and enable you to put your special stamp on a bit of the world.

name: The Animation Was 30 Seconds Long. The Client Paid $120 For It. It Took Three Hours to Make.
description: Most people see animated logos, social media adverts, YouTube intros, explainer videos, and app animations every day without giving them much thought. Businesses notice something else. They notice engagement. Attention. Brand recognition. Sales. That's why companies are willing to pay people who know how to bring static designs to life. And that's exactly what motion graphics is all about. Taking something ordinary and making it impossible to ignore. A logo becomes an animated brand reveal. A simple quote becomes a captivating video. A static social media post becomes content people stop scrolling for. And the person creating it gets paid. IMAGINE THIS... Imagine creating an animated logo for a business and watching it appear at the beginning of every video they publish. Imagine designing short social media animations that attract attention in crowded feeds. Imagine turning simple graphics, text, icons, and illustrations into professional visual content. Imagine having a skill that combines creativity, design, storytelling, and technology all in one. That's the opportunity motion graphics creates. And the demand continues to grow as more businesses compete for attention online. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN INSIDE • What motion graphics actually is and how it differs from traditional animation • The principles that make animation feel smooth, natural, and professional • How professional motion designers think and approach projects • Getting started with Adobe After Effects • Understanding compositions, layers, timelines, and workflows • The role of keyframes and why they're the foundation of animation • How to animate movement, scale, rotation, and opacity • The secret behind smooth animation using easing and the Graph Editor • Creating professional vector animations using shape layers • How Trim Paths create those satisfying line-drawing effects seen in professional work • Building animated icons, infographics, and visual elements • Creating kinetic typography where text itself becomes part of the storytelling • How to animate quotes, captions, headlines, and social media content • Logo animation techniques used by professional designers • Building memorable logo reveals and brand stings • Compositing techniques using masks, mattes, and blend modes • Character animation fundamentals • How motion graphics is used in social media marketing, explainer videos, and user interface design • Developing a portfolio that attracts potential clients • Turning your motion graphics skills into freelance opportunities WHY THIS SKILL MATTERS Every year, more businesses move online. More content is published. More brands compete for attention. And attention has become one of the most valuable resources on the internet. Motion graphics helps businesses earn that attention. A well-designed animation can explain an idea faster than a paragraph. It can make a brand look more professional. It can make content more engaging. It can make people stop scrolling. That's why businesses, agencies, content creators, and startups continue investing in motion design. PERFECT FOR • Creative individuals who enjoy design and visual storytelling • Students interested in digital media careers • Graphic designers looking to expand their skill set • Freelancers who want to offer higher-value services • Content creators and video editors • Social media managers • Entrepreneurs who want to create better content for their businesses • Anyone interested in learning a highly marketable digital skill THE TEENQUIP ADVANTAGE Many motion graphics tutorials assume you already have years of design experience. Others focus heavily on software while ignoring the creative principles that actually make animations look good. This guide takes a balanced approach. You'll learn the technical side. You'll learn the creative side. And you'll understand why professional animations work the way they do. Everything is explained in a practical, beginner-friendly way that helps you build confidence as you progress. WHAT MAKES MOTION GRAPHICS SO VALUABLE? Because businesses don't just want information. They want attention. A static image can communicate a message. But movement captures the eye. Movement creates emotion. Movement tells stories. And in a world where people scroll through hundreds of pieces of content every day, that matters. A lot. That's why skilled motion designers are involved in everything from advertising campaigns and social media content to mobile apps, television graphics, product launches, and brand identity projects. BY THE END OF THIS GUIDE... You'll understand the foundations of professional motion graphics, how animations are created, how designers bring ideas to life, and how businesses use motion to communicate more effectively. More importantly, you'll stop looking at animations as a viewer. You'll start understanding them as a creator. And once that shift happens, you'll begin seeing opportunities everywhere.
